newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, closely following U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, closely following U.S. mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose Thursday on the back of another boost to U.S. Treasuries after more economic indicators pointing to moderating U.S. growth.
"We had a trader-driven rise this session with U.S. markets," said a portfolio manager at a large Argentine bank. Argentine Brady bonds led the gains.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1-1/8 to 82-1/2, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.45 to 118.60.
Market players said activity continued to be very slim. "There really are no proper investors present," said the portfolio manager.
As the market continued to be one dominated by inter-bank trade, the high volatility seen all this week was also still present.
The dominating influence of U.S. Treasuries on the market was seen continuing, particularly with the all important U.S. jobs report due on Friday.

And with Argentine bonds seen slavishly following the U.S. in the days to come, the risks of a downturn are high if the U.S. market turns. "Note that the bearish spillover risks to the Brady market from Treasuries are high as volatility has risen," said analysts at financial consultancy I.D.E.A. in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.55 percent from 6.45 percent.
